name: Interval-aware kick + bass low end: pick bass notes that avoid semitone-adjacent clashes with the kick fundamental (move the bass up an octave), EQ out kick overtones that crowd the bass fundamental, saturate the kick so its harmonics land on octaves, then exciter and a mild transient expander to separate both in the mids
goal: Make kick and bass distinct by combining composition and processing, based on the physics that low notes are only a few Hz apart (E1 41.2 Hz vs F1 43.6 Hz, ~6% steps) so near-neighbour low notes beat and phase-cancel. Delta vs bass cluster (four-level kick+bass lock, short kick + 3 ducked subs): this one chooses bass pitches against the kick's tuned fundamental and overtones and shapes kick harmonics to octaves rather than relying on ducking.

source.title: The SCIENCE of Mixing Perfect Kick and Bass

prerequisites: A tuned kick (know or measure its fundamental note, e.g. with a spectrum analyser)
EQ, saturator, exciter and transient shaper/expander on kick and bass

inputs.name: kick
inputs.description: Kick drum with a measurable fundamental

inputs.name: bassline
inputs.description: Bass part to place against the kick

outputs.name: low_end
outputs.description: Kick + bass with fewer beating/phase-cancelling clashes and clearer mid-range identity

constraints: Use the 6%-per-semitone rule: in the lows adjacent semitones are only ~2-3 Hz apart and beat audibly; in the mids they are ~26 Hz apart.
Keep processing mild: transient expansion acts on roughly the first 50 ms; exciter and saturation are for distinction, not loudness.
Steady pitch only; no pitch-wobble tricks on kick or bass.

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Find the kick's fundamental note (e.g. E1 = 41.2 Hz) with an analyser and note its main overtones (e.g. F#2).
steps.expect: Kick fundamental and overtone notes written down

steps.action: Check where bass notes land on kick hits. If a bass note is a semitone or tone from the kick fundamental in the same octave (e.g. kick E1, bass F1), move the bass up an octave (F2) or re-voice it so it isn't adjacent.
steps.expect: No near-neighbour low notes sound together on kick hits

steps.action: If a kick overtone sits next to the bass fundamental (kick F#2 vs bass F2), cut that overtone on the kick with a narrow EQ bell.
steps.expect: Bass fundamental no longer beats against the kick

steps.action: Add a saturator to the kick so new harmonics are multiples of its fundamental (e.g. E3 above E1). These are more musical and clash less with the bass than the original stray overtone.
steps.expect: Kick has octave-related harmonics, sounds more distinct from bass

steps.action: Put an exciter on kick and on bass to add higher-order harmonics, lifting both into the mids and high mids where notes are far apart and phase cancellation is minor.
steps.expect: Each is identifiable in the mids

steps.action: Add a mild transient expander to kick and bass to emphasise the overtones in the first ~50 ms (attack/decay).
steps.expect: Clearer attacks; instruments separate without more low end

steps.action: A/B the low end in solo and in the mix; listen for periodic beating (the binaural-beat-like wobble) on simultaneous hits.
steps.expect: No steady beating on kick+bass hits; both distinct

verification: No kick hit coincides with a bass note within ~2 semitones of the kick fundamental in the same octave.
Spectrum shows kick harmonics at octave multiples after saturation and the clashing overtone reduced.
Solo low-pass (<150 Hz) shows no periodic beating on simultaneous hits.
